case_name: Vinaya Nair vs Corporation Of Cochin
facts_of_case: Petitioners, a Hindu husband and wife, married in accordance with the Hindu Marriage Act. They submitted an application to register their marriage but it was refused on the ground that the husband has Canadian domicile. Petitioners sought a writ of mandamus.

legal_principles.principle: Legislature would not envisage a situation where persons who are of Hindu religion, professes Hinduism, comes to a place where Hindu Marriage Act is applicable and solemnise their marriage, even then the marriage would not be treated as a valid marriage.
legal_principles.held: The Legislature in our view would not envisage a situation where persons who are of Hindu religion, professes Hinduism, comes to a place where Hindu Marriage Act is applicable and solemnise their marriage, even then the marriage would not be treated as a valid marriage even if they satisfied all the conditions laid down in the Hindu Marriage Act and followed all the customs.
cited_cases: Organo Chemical Industries Ltd. v. Union of India, AIR 1979 SC 1803
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — to determine the applicability of Hindu Marriage Act

legal_principles.principle: Legislative intent should not be reduced to futility by a bare mechanical interpretation.
legal_principles.held: The Apex Court held that a bare mechanical interpretation of the words and application of a legislative intent devoid of concept of purpose will reduce most of the remedial and beneficent legislation to futility.
cited_cases: Organo Chemical Industries Ltd. v. Union of India, AIR 1979 SC 1803
legal_principles.significance: MEDIUM — to emphasize the importance of considering legislative intent

outcome.final_order: The court held that the Hindu Marriage Act applies to a Hindu outside India if he is a Hindu domiciled in India, and not just those with permanent residence in India.
